correctness.rationale: For every finite connected positive-weight graph, the determinant forest partition function yields \(V_F=\sum_j q\lambda_j/(q+\lambda_j)^2\); diagonalizing the Gaussian kernel gives \(V_G=2\sum_j q^2/(q+\lambda_j)^2\). Completing the square in the exact difference, including Gaussian zero-mode variance \(2\), yields \(V_G-V_F=(25-n)/12+\frac1{12}\sum_{j=2}^n[(\lambda_j-5q)/(\lambda_j+q)]^2\). Equality forces all positive eigenvalues to be \(5q\); connectedness then forces \(L=5q(I-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n)\), so the graph has every edge with weight \(5q/n\). The complete-graph quadratic yields the precise reversal window. The included standard-library checker passed 612 exact rational assertions, including direct enumeration of rooted forests on small weighted trees; the all-dimensional proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The precise dimension-25 boundary and complete-graph uniqueness provide a sharp, non-asymptotic, graph-independent method-comparison benchmark for unmodified random-forest root-count and Gaussian quadratic-form inverse-trace estimators. The result identifies the first dimension permitting reversed one-draw variance and exact complete-graph regularization window. It makes no claim on runtime or on sign-probe/variance-reduced alternatives.
